source.title: Training Deep Neural Networks with Adaptive Momentum Inspired by the Quadratic Optimization
source.authors: Tao Sun; Huaming Ling; Z. Shi; Dong-Sheng Li; Bao Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests adaptive momentum on image classification and language modeling, including comparisons with standard optimizers, in settings beyond the cited optimizer-generalization studies.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out performance for Adam and AdamW alongside SGDM on CIFAR10, and SGDM alongside ASHB on ImageNet. The paper’s other optimizer comparisons do not directly compare adaptive methods with SGD and are not included as rows for V4.
record.test_reason: The study's CIFAR-10 results compare Adam and AdamW with momentum SGD on three PreResNet architectures, directly bearing on V4 under limited tuning. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their proposed adaptive momentum improves robustness to large learning rates, training speed, and generalization relative to the corresponding fixed-momentum baselines. They also establish convergence guarantees, but explicitly do not prove theoretical acceleration.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a newly proposed iteration-dependent adaptive momentum in SGD and Adam, rather than the optimizer comparisons in the original claim; tests CIFAR10 and ImageNet image classifiers and language tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and optimizer setting vary; the paper reports different results for CIFAR10 and ImageNet and compares Adam-style methods separately from SGDM/ASHB.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet, ASHB achieves 69.91% top-1 and 89.36% top-5 accuracy versus SGDM's 69.86% and 89.31%, with different learning rates and decay schedules.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapting heavy-ball momentum can match or slightly improve SGDM's held-out accuracy under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed adaptive-momentum Adam variants improve reported held-out performance over their Adam baselines on image and language tasks, including PTB perplexity of 60.9 versus 64.4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing fixed Adam momentum with the proposed adaptive momentum can improve held-out performance; these comparisons do not establish its standing relative to SGD.

record.problems: The direct Adam/AdamW versus SGDM accuracy comparisons use different initial learning rates, and Adam/AdamW learning rates were grid-searched while SGDM used benchmark settings. The ImageNet comparison reports SGDM versus ASHB, not Adam versus SGD.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer comparisons, including Ada2m and Ada2mW versus Adam and AdamW, are not direct adaptive-method versus SGD comparisons for V4. Training curves in Figures 3, 5, 6, and 7 were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Adaptive versus SGD comparisons on language tasks or ImageNet; broader hyperparameter tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; recovery attributable specifically to decoupled weight decay; equal or better training performance accompanying worse held-out performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the ImageNet limits_scope verdict: ASHB versus SGDM does not test V4's adaptive-learning-rate comparison. Other proposed-method comparisons and training curves are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. Conclusions use only the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Language benchmarks comparing Adam directly with SGD; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay as a recovery mechanism; switching from Adam to SGD.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness measures and their relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Adam and AdamW versus SGDM on CIFAR-10, PreResNet20/56/110, 200 epochs with the reported limited tuning.
relationships.reason: R1–R6 show lower test accuracy than SGDM throughout: Adam trails by 1.20–1.58 percentage points and AdamW by 0.98–1.70 points.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam and AdamW test accuracies than momentum SGD across the tested architectures remain unverified.
